rationale: Admin/maintainer permission metadata and product scope describe site deletion, not blanket authority to delete repository. Two methods are repository deletion or publishing source None; repository deletion is materially broader destructive action with separate authority/custody requirements. To delete via source, choose Deploy from a branch even when currently using Actions, then branch None and Save. This changes publishing mode/settings; do not treat as read-only or infer disabling all independent workflows without verification. Removing current deployment without deleting site is the distinct unpublish operation. Configuration/content retention and later redeployment differ from source None or repository deletion; recovery must match exact operation. No repository/site deleted, source changed or settings saved; linked repository-deletion procedure is not executed by ingestion. UI instructions are reference, not proof effective site unavailability, domain safety or accepted lifecycle policy. Full source and previously reviewed required include context read; source procedures not native behavior assurance.

rationale: Admin or maintainer can unpublish in FPT/GHEC/GHES source scope with plan-dependent Pages availability. Unpublishing removes current deployment and availability while preserving repository content/settings; it is not permanent site deletion or repository destruction. Unpublish procedure navigates repository then describes live-site Pages message/menu without explicitly repeating settings/Pages navigation. Preserve the procedural omission; screenshot/menu existence does not prove removal, access denial or authorization. Re-enable requires a new deployment: a successful site workflow run or selected branch publication with a commit. Generic successful unrelated workflow does not prove Pages deployment; require actual site deployment and behavior receipt. Unpublishing preserves publishing configuration, so subsequent authorized site workflow or branch change can republish. It is not a permanent publication-disable control or guaranteed prevention of accidental recovery. No site unpublished, workflow triggered, branch committed or native visibility changed. Linked publishing/deletion guides remain separately scoped; recovery availability, DNS/domain ownership and effective denied access remain unverified. Full source and previously reviewed required include context read; source procedures not native behavior assurance.
